# Fixed simplex caps: first-order rigidity and an explicit physical improvement

Let `d>=2`, `m=d+1`, and use barycentric coordinates in the affine
hyperplane `sum x_i=1`. The reference simplex has vertices `e_i` and
volume `V>0`. Fix thresholds `0<a_i<1` and the `m` caps

    H_i={x_i>=a_i},     Gamma_i=(1-a_i)^d.

No concurrence assumption is initially imposed. Nearby physical
simplices have the columns of `W` as their vertices, where every column
of `W` sums to one and `W` is near `I`. Their volume is `V det W`.
Write `F_i(W)` for their actual volume in the fixed cap `H_i`.

The conclusions are:

1. For arbitrary real multipliers `ell_i`, stationarity at `I` of
   `V det W-sum ell_i F_i(W)` holds if and only if all thresholds
   equal a common `a` and

       ell_i=1/[d(1-a)^(d-1)]                 for every i.       (1)

   In particular every stationary multiplier is strictly positive.

2. If the cap boundaries are concurrent, equivalently `sum a_i=1`,
   stationarity forces

       a_i=1/m,  ell_i=1/(m Gamma),  Gamma=(d/m)^d.              (2)

3. If the thresholds are not all equal, an explicit physical vertex
   velocity increases volume and decreases EVERY fixed cap volume
   strictly to first order. A sufficiently short actual simplex path
   therefore has larger volume and smaller mass in all the fixed caps.

These are local statements for the freely variable physical simplex.
They do not discard active Minkowski-inclusion constraints on a simplex
when it occurs as one fiber of a larger compatible family.

## 1. Exact derivative and the multiplier equations

Each fixed cap contains exactly its corresponding vertex in a
neighborhood of `I`. Its exact volume is

    F_i(W)/V = det W (W_ii-a_i)^d /
                       product_(j!=i)(W_ii-W_ij).              (3)

This follows by multiplying its `d` edge-intersection ratios. The
denominators and numerator are strictly positive near `I`.

Write `W=I+tB`, with every column sum of `B` zero. Let

    T=tr B,  b_i=B_ii,  s_i=sum_(j!=i) B_ij,
    k_i=d/(1-a_i)-m,  eta_i=ell_i Gamma_i.

Differentiating (3) gives

    F_i'(0)/V = Gamma_i [T+s_i+(1+k_i)b_i].                    (4)

Let `A` be the off-diagonal part of `B` and `c_j=sum_i A_ij`.
The column constraint gives `b_j=-c_j`. Thus all off-diagonal
entries `A_ij`, `i!=j`, are independent physical parameters.
The coefficient of `A_ij` in the Lagrangian derivative divided by `V`
is exactly

    -1+sum_l eta_l-eta_i+eta_j(1+k_j).                          (5)

If these coefficients all vanish, fix `j` and compare two distinct
indices `i,i'` different from `j`: then `eta_i=eta_i'`.
Because `m>=3`, this implies all `eta_i=e`. Equation (5) becomes

    -1+e(m+k_j)= -1+e d/(1-a_j)=0.

It follows that `e=(1-a_j)/d>0` for every `j`. Hence all thresholds
are equal, and (1) follows on dividing by `Gamma_j`. Conversely these
equal thresholds and multipliers make every coefficient in (5) zero.
This proves the full equivalence, even without a sign assumption on
the supplied multipliers.

## 2. Concurrence, coverage, zero multipliers, and dimension one

The `m` fixed boundary hyperplanes meet at a point of the barycentric
affine span if and only if `sum a_i=1`. Under this condition the common
point has barycentric coordinates `a_i`, and the caps cover the entire
affine span. Applying Section 1 gives (2).

More generally these caps cover the whole affine span if and only if
`sum a_i<=1`. If the sum is at most one, all coordinates cannot be
strictly below their respective thresholds. If the sum is greater than
one, the point with coordinates
`x_i=a_i-(sum a_l-1)/m` misses all caps. Its coordinates need not be
nonnegative: this is a statement about coverage of the affine span.

Consequently full-space coverage without concurrence is insufficient
for centroid rigidity. Every equal threshold `0<a<1/m` yields a
nonconcurrent full-space cover and the stationary positive multipliers
(1). For example in `d=2`, `a_i=1/4` and `ell_i=2/3` are stationary.

Zero multipliers cannot occur in a stationary objective-one certificate
in this freely variable simplex model. Section 3 also proves that the
cap derivative map is onto; hence an abnormal certificate with objective
coefficient zero has only the zero multiplier vector, even when real
signs are allowed.

The restriction `d>=2` in the rigidity claim is necessary. For `d=1`,
write the two independent off-diagonal velocities as `A_01,A_10`.
The normalized volume derivative is `-A_01-A_10`, while the two cap
derivatives are `-A_10,-A_01`, independently of the proper thresholds.
Stationarity therefore holds exactly for `ell_0=ell_1=1`, for EVERY
threshold pair. Concurrence does not force their common cut to be the
interval midpoint.

## 3. An explicit right inverse for all cap derivatives

Set

    h_i=d(1-a_i)^(d-1)>0.

For any desired normalized cap-derivative vector `f in R^m`, put

    z_i=f_i/h_i,   Z=sum_i z_i,
    S(f)_ii=z_i,
    S(f)_ij=z_i-Z/d                  for i!=j.                (6)

Every column of `S(f)` sums to zero. Its trace is `Z`.
Substituting into (4), its off-diagonal row sum is `d z_i-Z`, and
its normalized cap derivatives are

    Gamma_i [Z+d z_i-Z+(1+k_i)z_i]
       =Gamma_i(m+k_i)z_i=h_i z_i=f_i.

Thus (6) is a concrete right inverse of the full cap derivative map,
and

    tr S(f)=sum_i f_i/h_i.                                    (7)

Geometrically these velocities are combinations of a common dilation
and translation. No implicit constraint qualification is needed.

## 4. A constructive strict gain for nonuniform thresholds

Let `A_sum=sum_i a_i`. Define for `i!=j`

    J_ij=a_j+(a_i-A_sum)/d.                                   (8)

Not all these numbers vanish unless the thresholds are all equal:
comparing the equations for a fixed `j`, then using `m>=3`, proves
equality of all thresholds. For a nonuniform array choose any pair
with `J_ij!=0`, put `sigma=sign J_ij`, and use the elementary vertex
velocity `E` with only

    E_ij=sigma,  E_jj=-sigma

nonzero. Let `f(E)` be its normalized cap derivative vector (4).
The cap-neutral velocity

    B0=E-S(f(E))

has all cap derivatives zero. Its trace is

    tr B0=tr E-sum_l f_l(E)/h_l=|J_ij|=:J>0.                  (9)

For completeness, the coefficient of an arbitrary off-diagonal entry
`A_ij` in the linear functional
`tr B-sum_l f_l(B)/h_l` is exactly (8). This follows from (5) by
putting `eta_l=Gamma_l/h_l=(1-a_l)/d`; hence (9) includes the sign
and every dimensional factor.

Put

    H=sum_l 1/h_l,   epsilon=J/(2H),
    B=B0+S(-epsilon*1).                                      (10)

Then every column of `B` sums to zero, and

    tr B=J/2>0,       F_l'(0)/V=-epsilon<0 for every l.        (11)

For the actual path `W(t)=I+tB`, all determinants and cap edge factors
remain positive for sufficiently small `t>0`. Analyticity of (3) and
the strictly signed derivatives imply

    |W(t) simplex|>V,       F_l(W(t))<F_l(I) for every l.

This is an actual convex-simplex deformation and not just formal
independent changes of the cap volumes.

There is an important distinction in the statement: nonstationarity
for ONE specified multiplier vector does not imply this strict gain.
At equal thresholds the correct positive multipliers from (1) exist,
even if some other supplied multipliers are incorrect. Those correct
multipliers obstruct any direction that increases volume while all
cap derivatives are nonpositive. The strict gain construction applies
when NO multiplier vector can make stationarity hold, which here is
equivalent to nonuniform thresholds.

## 5. An exact rational concurrent example

In `d=2`, take `(a_0,a_1,a_2)=(1/2,1/3,1/6)`. Then
`h=(1,4/3,5/3)`, `J_01=1/12`, `H=47/20`, and
`epsilon=5/282`. Construction (10) produces a rational matrix `B`
with normalized volume derivative `1/24` and every normalized cap
derivative `-5/282`. At the rational time `t=1/100`, direct evaluation
of (3) verifies strict volume gain and strict decrease of all three
fixed cap volumes; every cap still contains exactly its designated
vertex.

The companion `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_simplex_fixed_cap_first_order_rigidity.py`
checks this physical witness, the exact derivative coefficients and
right inverse, nonuniform concurrent and nonconcurrent arrays, the
noncanonical equal-threshold stationary covers, and the `d=1` exception.
